title: Spherical Law of Cosines OQ-01: Vector Formalization on the Unit Sphere

problemStatement.formal: For unit vectors A, B, C on S^2, prove the spherical law of cosines through the identity cos(sideC) = cos(sideB) * cos(sideA) + <proj_perp(A,C), proj_perp(B,C)>.
problemStatement.plain: Formalizes spherical arc length and the inner-product decomposition behind the spherical law of cosines. The Lean file proves the algebraic and trigonometric forms for unit-vector spherical triangles.
whyMatters: Spherical trigonometry is the non-Euclidean analogue of the planar law of cosines.
The vector proof reduces the geometry to reusable inner-product and perpendicular-projection lemmas.
The metadata corrects a stale law-of-sines description and points search to the actual cosine-law theorem names.

proven: `arcLength_nonneg`, `arcLength_le_pi`, and `cos_arcLength` establish the basic arc-length facts for unit vectors.
`norm_projectPerp_sq_eq_sin_sq` and `norm_projectPerp_eq_sin` connect perpendicular projections with sine of arc length.
`spherical_law_of_cosines_algebraic` proves the core inner-product decomposition form.
`degenerate_triangle_sideB_zero` records a degenerate-case check and `planar_law_of_cosines` documents the planar comparison.
`SphericalLawOfCosines.lean` is recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: A fully normalized angle form replacing the projection inner product with sin(a)sin(b)cos(C) is not separated as the main theorem here.
The small-angle planar limit is documented rather than proved as an asymptotic theorem.
knownResults.goal: Expose the proved vector formalization of the spherical law of cosines with accurate searchable metadata.
